utilization_model: Idealized duty cycle rises as active runtime increases for fixed planned gap.
Actual duty cycle must use actual close and next-start timestamps because overshoot consumes planned gap.
Wake jitter can turn a nominal +3m plan into a much larger idle gap.
A longer target that increases close-loss probability can reduce expected useful throughput despite higher nominal duty cycle.
Therefore operating cap optimization is a reliability-adjusted utilization problem.
Incremental durable checkpoints reduce expected lost work from abrupt termination but add write overhead.
Checkpoint cadence itself may later be optimized once boundary behavior is understood.
During boundary search, evidence cadence should favor observability over micro-optimizing write overhead.
Pre-arm scheduling shifts continuation protection earlier and removes a fragile late scheduler operation.
Planned-gap optimization should occur only after runtime cap is stable enough to avoid interaction confounds.
Intentional parallel successors can later raise aggregate utilization beyond single-owner duty cycle but require duplicate-work fencing.
The current strict phase correctly postpones that optimization.
